newsitem.title: USA: CME nearby hogs rally ahead of report, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME nearby hogs rally ahead of report, end mixed.

text.p: Nearby CME hog futures rallied on late short covering and buy stops and deferreds held losses ahead of the Hogs and Pigs report while pork belly futures closed mixed, traders said.
Hog futures closed 1.025 cent per lb higher to 0.925 lower with July up 0.575 at 82.825 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.125 higher to 1.000 lower with only July up at 82.225 cents.

A firmer tone to cash hogs and some concern the report may not show nearby hog numbers as large as anticipated boosted nearby hog futures into buy stops. Deferreds declined on expectations there will still be herd expansion, they said.
Technicals also point to a stronger chart picture in nearbys, they added.

Analyst estimates on Friday's quarterly report put June 1 all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms at an average 102.9 percent of a year ago and ranged from 101.7 to 105 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 104.3 percent in a range of 103 to 106 percent and hogs kept for market averaged 102.6 percent of a year ago in a range of 101 to 105 pct.

R.J. O'Brien and Rand Financials were light buyers early while LFG, Smith Barney and Lind-Waldock were light sellers. In hog options, there was scattered buying of puts and calls ahead of the report, pit sources said.

Nearby pork belly futures showed pressure much of the day from profit taking despite further strength in cash bellies. Deferreds found short covering support. Trade was very light as evening up ahead of the report dominated the market, traders said.
Cash bellies were up again at noon with 14-16 lbs at $86 per cwt, highest since June 6.

Strength in cash bellies came despite the larger pace of slaughter this week. This shows good slicer interest and possible increased retailer featuring of bacon going into the the summer bacon-lettuce-tomato-sandwich season, they added.
